comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar (Type 48) at 895 Bush St in RC-4, approved July 2014, 157 meters away. Same corridor, same zoning, same license type.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This agency referral was approved within 10 days because it was for an existing bar use (Stookey's Club Moderne). The pattern on this corridor is that existing bar uses are routinely approved, while new conversions—especially from protected uses like laundromats—face discretionary review.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar (Type 42, beer/wine) at 845 Bush St in RC-4, approved January 2003, 110 meters away. Same block and zoning district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved this Type 42 referral for a bar in RC-4, citing that bar use is permitted on the ground floor per Planning Code Sections 209.8(c)/218(b). However, as an agency referral it does not address whether a laundromat conversion would be allowed; the approval confirms the use is permitted in the abstract but does not waive Section 202.12.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar (Type 48) at 925 Bush St in RC-4, approved January 2019, 224 meters away. Transfer of existing bar use in the same zoning district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This Type 48 transfer was approved for an existing bar. The description explicitly states 'Continuation of existing use,' confirming that transfers of existing bar licenses in RC-4 are straightforward, while new bar uses replacing other uses—especially laundromats—require a CUA.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA for a restaurant and bar at 532–536 Sutter St in C-3-R, 73 meters away, filed April 2013 and withdrawn April 2015 after two years. This is the only true use-decision case (not an agency referral) among nearby bar applications in the last decade.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The applicant withdrew this CUA to convert an assembly hall to a restaurant and bar after two years of processing. While the record does not state a reason, the withdrawal illustrates the time, cost and uncertainty of a discretionary hearing for a new bar use in this area. This is the path 779 Bush now faces.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar (Type 48) at 580 Sutter St in C-3-R, approved February 2022, 58 meters away. Recent approval in a nearby downtown commercial district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved this Type 48 agency referral in three weeks because it was a continuation of an existing bar use. Even in a district where bar use is principally permitted, Planning emphasized 'Continuation of existing use,' reinforcing that new conversions—particularly from protected uses—are treated differently.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain written confirmation from SF Planning that Section 202.12 requires a CUA for this laundromat conversion.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a pre-application meeting or zoning letter from the SF Planning Department, citing the September 8, 2022 agency referral denial at 779 Bush St (case 2022-008099MIS) and asking whether a Conditional Use Authorization under Planning Code Section 202.12 is still required for a laundromat-to-bar conversion, and whether any other discretionary approvals apply. Bring the project description, floor plan and photographs of the existing space. Do not file or pay for any other application until you have this answer in writing.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for health permit to operate after DPH plan check is approved and construction is substantially complete.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the health permit application online with the Business Account Number (BAN), Location ID and federal EIN at least one month before the planned opening. Confirm that a certified food safety manager is on staff (ServSafe or equivalent) and that all employees will obtain California food handler cards within 30 days of hire. Schedule the pre-opening inspection with DPH at about 80% construction complete to catch any issues early, then schedule the final inspection for after all equipment, finishes and hot water are in place. The permit is issued after the final inspection passes.

filing_playbook.action: Complete all business formation, registration, tax and insurance filings before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State; obtain the federal EIN from the IRS online; register for a California seller's permit with CDTFA; register as an employer with EDD; obtain workers' compensation insurance; register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector and file a fictitious business name statement with the County Clerk if the public name differs from the entity name. Also register for RBS training through the ABC portal and ensure every alcohol server and manager completes certification within 60 days of hire. Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI licences for recorded music before opening.

records_summary: The records show a significant obstacle at this address: an ABC Type 48 (bar) referral was denied by Planning in September 2022—two months ago—because Planning Code Section 202.12 requires a Conditional Use Authorization to change the use of a laundromat, even though bar use is principally permitted on the ground floor in the RC-4 zoning district. The block is densely developed with alcohol uses: 24 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft (92 within 1,000 ft) and 5 bars within 500 ft. Nearby bar approvals in RC-4 (801 Bush, 845 Bush, 895 Bush) were for continuations of existing bar uses or transfers, not new conversions requiring discretionary review.
data_gaps: No hearing records or decision text available for the September 2022 denial to understand Planning's full reasoning
No conditions data extracted from nearby bar approvals to understand typical operating restrictions
Census tract undue-concentration status for ABC purposes not confirmed by the records
No discretionary review history available for other laundromat conversions in RC-4 to gauge hearing outcomes
